fields.heading: A corner shop that stops footfall

html:
Study facts

  • Scope Interior of a small corner shop
  • Key move Entry, display and till in one triangle
  • Lighting Layered zones for window, hero wall and ambient

Illustrative design study. Not built work, not a client project.

The brief

The shop sits on a corner with good footfall and a cramped floor. Stock blocks the window, and customers never reach the back wall.

We treat the corner as a stage. The window pulls people in, the display wall holds them, and the checkout sits where sightlines naturally end.

The moves

  • Window as invitation. A shallow, lit display band at eye level turns the corner glass into a pause point, not a wall of boxes.
  • The display wall. One long, well-lit wall carries hero products. Everything else stays shallow so the shop breathes.
  • The checkout triangle. Entry, display and till form a triangle. Staff see the whole floor and customers never wander.
  • Light that sells. Layered lighting separates window, hero wall and ambient, so each zone does its job at any hour.

Takeaways

Design corners from the pavement in.

A checkout you can see is a checkout you will reach.

Less stock on display usually sells more.
A checkout you can see is a checkout you will reach.
